kultivator.screen.help.duel_pedang.title: Sword Duel
kultivator.screen.help.duel_pedang: The Sword Duel is the blade-clash mechanic. Open Scroll › World › Sword Duel, or /cultivate duel tantang [entity] [bebas|handicap|tekan]: choose an opponent, the rules (Free, Handicap, Realm Press) and a stake; the opponent answers with accept or refuse. Nobody dies: a duel stops at 10%% health. Win at the 10%% line, with a Deathblow, by a ring-out, or when the opponent yields. Left click slashes in the direction the mouse moves, hold for a heavy slash, sneak + click to thrust. A right click with a weapon (off hand empty) or [[key:parry]] deflects just before the blade lands; hold to guard. A deflect in the last 100 milliseconds is a Perfect Deflect: the opponent recoils and you get an Opening. Deflects, clashes and guarding fill the Posture bar; a full bar is a Posture Break (staggered 1.5 seconds, the 決 mark), and an attack then is a Deathblow. Two heavy slashes that meet lock the blades: click repeatedly to push, or deflect just as the opponent pushes hard for a Sudden Release. The red 危 mark comes before a perilous attack: Mountain Cleave (deflect, do not guard), Death Thrust (only a Perfect Deflect) and Low Sweep (jump or dodge). Sparring (/sect spar), sparring with a wanderer in town, sect tournament bouts and disciples' Honour Duels all use these rules. Watch Duel (/cultivate duel murid) sets two of your disciples against each other without a stake; change the view with [[key:duel_camera]]. Its settings are spread over the Settings groups: sparks and blade trails (Display & Effects), camera and intro (Camera & Film), kiai and cheers (Sound), posture bars (HUD), input, deflect outside duels and lock-on (Controls).
kultivator.screen.help.sekte_hidup.title: The Living Sect
kultivator.screen.help.sekte_hidup: Once a Sect Hall stands, your disciples live their own lives. Its cards are in Scroll › Disciples › Roster (locked until you have a Sect Hall); Disciple Moods and the Stair Record are in Scroll › Disciples; its commands are under /cultivate perguruan. Its ten parts: (1) Character and loyalty: every disciple has two or three traits and contentment 0-100; a neglected disciple turns Restless, then Defiant, then prepares to leave; talk, give gifts or apologise before the Hall Stele. (2) Ties: disciples drink tea together and become friends, rivals or enemies; an Honour Duel can turn a grudge into rivalry. (3) Tournaments on the Lei Tai ring (see the Lei Tai Tournament topic). (4) The Thousand-Step Trial Stair: candidates climb an illusory stair; older disciples may climb again for 200 PK, once every 30 days. (5) The Scripture Pavilion and the Ancestral Altar: disciples read technique scrolls from the shelves; the fallen are buried, and incense and the Qingming rite every 15 days calm the disciples' hearts. (6) Elders and the Heir: Elder-rank disciples hold offices, run daily affairs and report every morning; a strong heir can be crowned second-generation Sect Master. (7) Story Missions: a team leaves the sect and comes home through the gate with a written report, sometimes bringing a candidate or a treasure. (8) Emblem, Robes and Banners. (9) Diplomacy with NPC sects (see the Sect Diplomacy topic). (10) Garden and Mine (see the Garden & Mine topic). No block ever changes: new buildings come only through Sect Construction.
kultivator.screen.help.turnamen_sekte: The weekly tournament (see the Tournament topic) moves to the arena stage once you build the Lei Tai Tribune: raise the hall to template 6 or higher on the Build page, then build its component (Sect Construction tier 7) from the materials you deposit. Every bout is a 90-second Sword Duel in a 6-block ring (the final 30 seconds longer, with an opening film) that stops at 10%% health; an empty-handed disciple borrows a sword. Idle disciples, villagers and envoys of other sects watch from the tribune and cheer. Every disciple who ever fought is listed on this season's Elo board (starting at 1000; the board keeps 30 names and the last 12 champions). NPC sects sometimes challenge you: accept or refuse with a click in chat, the Tournament card, or /cultivate perguruan turnamen terima|tolak. Accepted, 4 of their disciples join the bracket as guests and two of their envoys watch; a win raises that sect's standing with you by 10, a loss lowers it by 10, refusing lowers it by 3, and an unanswered challenge lapses after 3 days at no cost. The old tournament's rewards and schedule are unchanged.
kultivator.screen.help.diplomasi_sekte: NPC sects have their own mountain gates in the world, grow and wage war on each other. Find them through Story Missions, envoys, or by visiting their gate; everything is on the Sect Diplomacy card (Scroll › Sect › Living Sect). Each sect's standing with you runs from −100 to 100: war below −70 (once declared), hostile below −30, cold below −10, neutral below 20, friendly above. An envoy (the Elder of Outer Affairs or an idle Golden Core+ disciple) is away one day and returns with standing +5 (+3 for the Elder) and the location of their gate; 3 days between envoys. From standing 20 you may propose a pact: no raids, no luring of disciples and no mission ambushes from them. From 60 (not a demonic path) they can become allies: two guards come when your hall is raided, a weekly PK gift and joint tournaments. A much stronger hall can demand tribute. A hostile sect can declare war and raid every 3-5 days; win the war by beating their master at their mountain gate (or in your hall after their letter of challenge). Three raids that plunder mean defeat: forced tribute, never blocks or disciples. Peace is accepted when they are weaker, you won two raids, or the war has lasted 12 days.
kultivator.screen.help.kebun_tambang: Spirit Herb Plots need template 2 or higher, then their component (Sect Construction tier 3); the Spirit Mine Mouth needs template 4 or higher and its tier-4 component, on the sect's hillside. Open the Garden & Mine card (Scroll › Sect › Living Sect), or click a plot's soil or the mine mouth in the world. Plant spirit herbs in the plots; the disciples assigned to them tend them every day, and a plot in bloom is harvested with a click. Miners go in by shifts: one shift = one world day, and the yield (spirit stones, ore, sometimes a find from the mountain's belly) goes into the Granary when the day turns. The deeper the mine's level, the richer the yield and the greater the danger. A disciple worked past the limit of days without rest counts as forced labour, and that lowers their contentment. Nothing is really planted and no block is dug: it all happens in the hall's data. (The Hundred Herb Garden of Sect Construction tier 2 is a different building; see the Glossary.)
kultivator.screen.help.suara.title: Sound and Music
kultivator.screen.help.suara: Settings › Sound. Cinematic music plays a stretch of vanilla music for your own moments and follows the music slider; Aura hum is the low per-realm hum of auras near you (the Ambient slider). Japanese spoken voices (VOICEVOX): All, Heaven only, or Off; their volume follows the vanilla Voice/Speech slider. Voice captions show who speaks, the translation and the original Japanese at the bottom of the screen. Click the Voice credits row to hear a sample and the name of every voice. For the Sword Duel: Kiai (your own shout on heavy slashes, Deathblows and won blade locks) and the crowd's cheers in the arena. All of this is saved on your computer only.
kultivator.screen.help.hud.title: Kultivator HUD
kultivator.screen.help.hud: Settings › HUD. The Kultivator HUD coin hides or shows every Kultivator display on screen: the dantian orb, realm and qi, the guide tracker, the Technique Codex and cooldowns, elite plates, the building HUD, the Stair, the Lei Tai, the ship panel, dragon stamina, sky chips, the Elder report and the wound line. Every HUD uses one jade slip style with full-size text. News (results, duel offers, finished chapters, the morning report) shows as cards at the top right, at most three at once; under them one right-side event scroll shows one thing at a time (Joining Exam, Lei Tai, Stair, Gate Defence, then the Guide) and the rest wait. On narrow screens the less important lines beside the dantian orb hide first. The tribulation warning and the soul timer always show, because both concern your life; the formation alarm keeps showing while Danger alert is on. Danger alert: while meditating, a bell, a reddening screen edge and the names of monsters in sight within 12 blocks. Cooldown reminder: a chime and a seal glint when a cooldown of 10 seconds or more ends. Guide: the First Steps tracker on the right edge (needs the server connection). Posture bars over heads moves duel opponents' Posture bars from the top of the screen to above each fighter's head.
kultivator.screen.help.tombol.title: Keys and Controls
kultivator.screen.help.tombol: Settings › Controls holds the only list of Kultivator keys. Click a row (or select it and press Enter), press the new key, and it is set and saved at once; Esc cancels, Backspace or Delete unbinds it, a middle or side mouse button works too, a right click restores the default. A key another binding also uses is red with that binding's name. All Minecraft keys… opens the vanilla controls screen for the game's own keys. The defaults: G casts the selected technique (hold for the Seal Wheel), V Quick Access (tap: the Scroll, hold: the wheel), B meditate, Z next technique, H flying sword, M Disciples, K Technique Codex, J Guide, N Map, Backspace skips a cinematic. The Scroll, World, Ring and Immortality keys are unbound on purpose (reached through Quick Access); previous technique and quick seals 1-4 through the Seal Wheel; the Sword Duel deflect is a right click with a weapon. Inside the Scroll: 1-8 sections, Q/E pages, Tab focus, / search, Esc back. Texts in the Guide Book and Encyclopedia always name your current key. This group also holds how casting works (hold and release), the Sword Duel input (Automatic, Classic, Vanilla), deflect outside duels, lock-on, the Player Animation Library animations and Hardcore breakthroughs (switching it on asks for confirmation).
kultivator.screen.help.glosarium.title: Glossary
kultivator.screen.help.glosarium: Words that used to name two things. Scroll: the Cultivation scroll is this screen (tap Quick Access); paths are written Scroll › section › card. Realms: True Immortal is the peak of the mortal world, not "True Immortal God"; Foundation Establishment. Tribulation: heaven's lightning trial, also the Spirit Beast Tribulation. Decree: only the decrees of the Heavenly Decree Seal (Scroll › Immortality › Heavenly Decree); the tasks of the Jade Palace envoys in the Immortal City are Envoy Orders. Missions: Expeditions are the daily board on the hall's Missions tablet (send 1-3 disciples); Story Missions are the Living Sect's storied missions; the Mission Board in town gives tasks for yourself. The Offering Office (formerly the Mission Office) in the hall trades offered goods for PK; it holds no missions. Duels: the Sword Duel is the mechanic; Sparring, wanderer sparring, tournament bouts and Honour Duels all use it. Sects: a sect with disciples is founded with the Sect Hall Stele; /sect only forms a Sect Fellowship, a group of players without disciples; NPC sects have their own mountain gates. Renown: the hall's good name. Elders: Grand Elder is a disciple rank; the leading seat in the Elder Hall is the office of Steward Elder. Rivals: the Rival Groups (Scroll › World › Rivals) hunt you; a rival disciple is a tie between disciples. Towers: the Hundred-Floor Tower is a ruin in the world; the Blazing Sky Tower is a tier-9 hall building. Gardens: the Hundred Herb Garden is a tier-2 hall building; the Spirit Herb Plots belong to Garden & Mine; the Immortal Peach Garden is in the Immortal City. Natal Treasure: the forged treasure you absorb; a disciple's is a Disciple's Natal Treasure. Destruction: Destruction Mode (Self Destruction) is your own choice and, with your disciples' Destroyer Arts under the Red Seal, the only thing that changes blocks; without it every effect is visual only.
